text:
Erin: Heads up — since the 14:00 deploy we're seeing long queue tails and weird GPU distribution on eu-west clusters. head-of-line jobs are tiny but blocking big batches behind them.
Jamal: Uptime graf shows nodepool-a GPUs ~30% utilized while queue length ~800. that mismatch smells like admission order problem.
Niko: Can you paste scheduler logs for a blocked admission? here are a couple lines I grabbed:
```
2026-03-14T14:02:12Z scheduler.INFO admit request id=job-0a3 wait_ms=4200 gang=1 preferred_node_group=nodepool-a
2026-03-14T14:02:12Z scheduler.WARN head_of_line block job=job-0a3 reason=affinity_mismatch pending_after=7
2026-03-14T14:02:13Z scheduler.INFO admission skipped job=job-1b7 reason=head_of_line
```
Erin: exact. small job with strict node affinity sits at front of the queue; all following multi-GPU batches can't be dispatched even though capacity exists on other nodes.
Sasha: Is the redispatch/skip-on-affinity-fail path supposed to run? I thought we had logic to try 3 alternative nodes before blocking.
Jamal: looks like that path only runs for gang_size>1. bug: single-node jobs are treated as atomic and never requeued for alternative nodes.
Niko: repro steps I used:
```
# create affinity job that binds to missing label
curl -XPOST $SCHED/api/v1/submit -d '{"job": {"id":"job-0a3","affinity":"gpu-rtx-locked","gpus":1}}'
# submit a few large batches behind it
for i in 1 2 3; do curl -XPOST $SCHED/api/v1/submit -d '{"job": {"id":"batch-$i","gpus":8}}'; done
```
Sasha: Confirmed locally. scheduler's admission loop checks head_of_line and then applies a rate limiter token bucket; the token bucket doesn't decrement when skipping, so the blocker consumes admission tokens repeatedly.
Erin: That's painful — a single mis-targeted job draining rate tokens causing backpressure across the whole region.
infra-bot: incident-created:INC-2026-1123 assigned to eng-infra
opsbot: deploy rollback recommended if immediate relief needed
Jamal: short-term mitigation options:
- mark offending affinity label as quarantined so scheduler will not honor (manual)
- increase admission token bucket burst (fast config change)
- rollback last scheduler commit (if we want safe immediate fix)
Niko: long-term fix: implement head-of-line skip that both requeues to tail and decrements a separate fail counter; also ensure skip path consumes a token only once per job. add test: 500 simulated single-node blockers with mixed batch sizes to assert utilization >80%.
Sasha: also propose a metric: head_of_line_block_duration and per-label blocker_count — we have no visibility today.
Erin: Can someone open a PR with the fix + unit tests? put in a canary gate with redispatch enabled by flag. I'll do the canary infra changes.
Jamal: I'll handle emergency config bump (admission.tokens.burst) and add the metric to the console dashboard.
Niko: PR stub: https://git.internal/r/redwood/scheduler/pulls/3892 (WIP) — tagged @Sasha @Erin
Sasha: ack. I'll review and add the telemetry.
Erin: thanks all. keeping this thread updated. if utilization doesn't improve in 15m we'll rollback.
notes: Thread about scheduler head-of-line blocking causing uneven GPU utilization and admission token exhaustion. Contains logs, repro steps, mitigation plan, and action items.
